title: The Book of Divine Consolation of the Blessed Angela of Foligno
author: Angela of Foligno (c. 1248-1309), recorded by her confessor Brother Arnaldo
translator: Mary G. Steegmann; introduction by Algar Thorold
edition_cited: London: Chatto and Windus, 1909 (New Medieval Library). archive.org scan divineconsolatio00angeuoft
locator_hints: Treatise III, 'Visions of the Sacrament of the Altar', first to seventh (printed pp. 222-231; about lines 8565-8880): seeing in the Host a beauty 'more splendid than the sun', 'two eyes of great splendour'
Treatise III, visions of God 'in darkness' (lines 7170-7300)
Treatise I ch. I (line 1514) on being thrown into 'horrible darkness of spirit'
summary: Angela's dictated account of her conversion and visions. The passages nearest the brief are the seven 'visions of the Sacrament of the Altar': while looking at the elevated Host during Mass she says she saw 'with mine eyes' Christ in it, sometimes a throat 'more splendid and beauteous than the sun', sometimes 'two eyes of great splendour, and so large that I beheld nothing of the Host save the edge thereof'. Elsewhere she describes seeing God 'in a darkness' which she ranks above all the luminous visions. The practice context is penance, long prayer, and fixed looking at the Host or crucifix; no method is offered to others, and nothing is said to someone who sees nothing.
why_relevant: Open-eye testimony of light and form seen on a fixed object of gaze during liturgy, with what she was doing; and a counter-valuation of 'darkness' over light.

notes: Steegmann translates an Italian version of 1536, not the critical Latin Memorial; wording differs from modern translations (Lachance 1993).
